requirement:
The harness MUST stop retrying a completion request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` when the next attempt would
start more than one minute after the first of its consecutive transient
failures, including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point.
It MUST then fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts
and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.
rationale:
structural: Every clause in `requirements.authoring.provider_backoff.limit` describes observable behavior only. It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or interface that the implementation must use.

- "MUST stop retrying a completion request ... when the next attempt would start more than one minute after the first of its consecutive transient failures, including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point." A harness could track a deadline, compare elapsed time, or precompute a cumulative delay budget. All of these stop at the same moment, so the choice is discretionary.
- "MUST then fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available." This is an output obligation. Any error construction or formatting that carries those facts satisfies it.
- The parent `requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` is cited only for context. It also states behavior, such as the retry classification, window doubling, jitter, `Retry-After` handling, and disabled SDK retries. Those obligations belong to that requirement, not to this one.

No structural obligation needs implementation evidence here. The review roots are empty, so the absence of implementation edges is not a gap. Tests supply the behavioral evidence.

behavioral: The one reviewed test, `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[retrying_stops_once_a_request_has_failed_for_a_minute]`, is marked {test} for the subject. It covers each obligation of `requirements.authoring.provider_backoff.limit`.

**Stop when the next attempt would start more than one minute after the first consecutive transient failure**
- A simulated clock runs repeated 429 `ThrottlingException` failures through `ProviderBackoff::retry`. Every `Wait` is asserted to leave `now <= start + 60s`. The loop must end in `Stop`, and more than 3 attempts must occur. This exercises the randomized window delays up to the limit.
- Boundary: a second failure at +58s must still `Wait` with a delay of at most 2s. That puts the next attempt at or before the one-minute mark, so retrying is allowed.
- `Retry-After` of 60 on the first failure waits exactly 60s. `Retry-After` of 61 stops. This pins the boundary for a provider delay.
- `Retry-After` of 90 stops at once. This covers the case where a provider delay passes the limit.
- The limit is measured from the first failure. The last-failure cases make the first failure at `start + RETRY_LIMIT` and the second at `start + 3*RETRY_LIMIT`. The second call must `Stop`, so the limit is relative to the first failure rather than to an absolute time.
- A permanent 400 `ValidationException` stops with its own error. That error lacks "kept failing", so the limit path applies only to transient failures.

**Failure error names the attempt count and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available**
- The 429 loop asserts the message contains "after {attempts+1} attempts" and "HTTP 429 ThrottlingException". This covers the attempt count and both status and code.
- Partial information is covered by three cases. Status only (503) gives "last failure: HTTP 503". Code only gives "last failure: ThrottlingException". A timeout with no status or code gives "last failure: no response within ten minutes".

I found no obligation without a test. Whether the returned `Stop` error is then reported as the assessment failure belongs to the wider provider_backoff behavior. It is not an independent observable obligation of this limit rule.

text: :::{req} provider_backoff.limit
The harness MUST stop retrying a completion request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` when the next attempt would
start more than one minute after the first of its consecutive transient
failures, including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point.
It MUST then fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts
and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.
:::{req} provider_backoff
When a provider reports a transient failure, the harness MUST wait and retry
the same completion request. Transient failures are throttling, reported
through HTTP 429 or a Bedrock `ThrottlingException`; temporary unavailability,
reported through HTTP 500, 502, 503, or 504 or a Bedrock
`ServiceUnavailableException`, `InternalServerException`, or
`ModelNotReadyException`; and a request with no response after ten minutes,
which the harness MUST abandon. The retry MUST retain its prompt, history,
tools, and pending inputs. It MUST NOT
restart the assessment or repeat already completed tool calls. A permanent
input/context-length error, authentication failure, or invalid request MUST
remain an error; mentioning tokens in an error message alone MUST NOT trigger
retries.
The backoff window MUST start at one second and double after each consecutive
transient failure, up to sixty seconds. Each delay MUST be randomly selected
between half and all of that window to spread parallel retries. An available
provider `Retry-After` value, in seconds or HTTP-date form, MUST be honored as a
minimum delay even when longer than the window. A successful response MUST reset
backoff for the next completion request, and interruption MUST cancel both the
wait and further retries.
Each attempt MUST count toward the assessment totals under {cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_requests`.
Hidden SDK retries MUST remain disabled so the harness can account for attempts.
Transient retries MUST NOT be reported as finished judgments or terminal
assessment errors while recovery is still in progress. Pending inputs MUST be
recorded as evidence only after the request succeeds.
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider` {cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`
